No, we can't certify that. What we can say is narrower: NASA FIRMS recorded no thermal detections intersecting the asset (ASSET-F06) between 2026-10-06 and 2026-11-05. All four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS) covered every day of that period, so the lack of detections isn't a coverage gap.

However, the tool explicitly states this does not establish that no fire occurred. Small, short-lived, cool or cloud-obscured fires can go undetected, particularly at 375 m (VIIRS) and 1 km (MODIS) resolution. The result also says nothing about burned area, the cause of any change, or anything outside the period.

A suitable statement would be: "No FIRMS thermal anomalies were detected within the asset during the period, with full sensor coverage." If you need stronger assurance, you'd want complementary evidence such as burned-area mapping or high-resolution imagery. Note that the data is near real time, so it reflects knowledge as of 2026-11-12.
